instruction_review: Self-contained one-period market, timing, primitive units, quasilinear welfare, observable fixed emission mapping, physical capacities and fixed participants specified.

Feasible uniform tax and equal nontradable firm standard distinguished from subsidies, discriminatory instruments and permit markets. Administration is a real fixed cost for any deployed instrument; no intervention is separately available at zero cost.

Government receipts, private profits, consumer surplus, external harm and net cash reconcile to resource surplus without double-counted transfers or administration. A stipulated lump-sum public numeraire endowment funds negative public cash; compensation of losers is not asserted.

Competitive price-taking benchmark distinguished from two-firm Cournot incentives. Strict concavity, clipped-response contraction and active-set lower/interior/upper inequalities supply global output results.
Best feasible policies exhaust every valid affine policy interval, all endpoints/stationary points and fixed administration/no-policy comparisons. The plotted tax grid is not used for optimization.

All seven scenarios and both conduct regimes solved, including low/high damage, tax upper boundary, physical upper boundaries, inactive-firm zero boundary, high administration and a fully solved asymmetric allocation/standard comparison.

Asymmetric Cournot uniform taxes preserve a 12-unit firm-output difference while the efficient allocation requires 24; efficient total output therefore need not imply efficient productive allocation. Excluded discriminatory taxes are diagnostic only.

Fixed baseline-policy stress results are separated from scenario-specific reoptimization. Ex ante uncertainty fixes the policy before damage is observed, uses stipulated probabilities and reconciles the weighted state ledger; no estimated uncertainty or adaptive-policy claim.
Complete deliverables and 100-point rubric with five 20-point domains/four five-point criteria each; 85 overall and 15 per domain stated as author criteria, critical errors require revision.

Instructor guide supplies baseline ledgers/incidence, every recommended policy/welfare target, full asymmetric standard branches, all boundary explanations, uncertainty targets and open-response evidence criteria.

Identification plan distinguishes equilibrium correlation, structural primitives, policy assignment, exposure/harm measurement and welfare valuation. It supplies concrete timing, confounding and post-treatment-control critiques without inventing data.

resolved_findings.finding: Root noted that the competitive maximization characterization must include the deployed tax and effective bounds.
resolved_findings.resolution: Corrected to B−sum C−tQ over the effective output box including standards; planner target remains B−sum C−D over physical bounds. Checker requires the corrected objective text.

source_policy: Three existing accepted primary-method IDs reused with original inspection scopes and explicit project_reuse fields. No duplicate catalogue IDs or new empirical findings proposed.
limitations: Independent scalar roots and affine incentive certificates verify the supplied two-firm convex model and feasible instruments; they do not validate real conduct, demand, cost, damage or enforcement assumptions.
Unweighted quasilinear welfare and lump-sum finance are stipulated criteria/assumptions. Neither a welfare increase nor this checker establishes Pareto compensation or ethical agreement.
The uncertainty exercise permits damage changes only, with supplied weights and a single ex ante instrument. It is not estimation, a confidence interval or an adaptive policy experiment.
Source records reuse accepted chapter primary inspections; project parameters, examples and proofs are original. No empirical dataset or current legal assertion is embedded.

Human-readable proof, prompt/answer and policy interpretation still require editorial review. Root retains volume acceptance, integration and publication; no visual/mobile/print UI QA or external human certification is claimed.
acceptance: Complete authored project package submitted; no shared curriculum/checkpoint/build/hosting files changed. Root owns volume acceptance, integration and publication.
